intro: You have come to Comana, an ancient city in Adana province, whose story runs from the 2nd millennium BC to the 6th century AD. This was a temple city of the Mother Goddess Ma, linked to the Hittite city of Kummanni.
history: Comana is identified with the Kummanni of Hittite records. In classical times it ruled a great temple-state of the Mother Goddess Ma. Under Rome it was called a 'holy city', and according to Strabo it was home to more than six thousand sacred attendants. Imagine the bustle of so many serving one goddess.
structure-1: You are now at the Main Temple, the chief cult building, dedicated to the city's principal deity. Pause here: this was the heart of the temple city.
structure-2: Here are the Sanctuary Remains: the surviving traces of sacred precincts dedicated to the gods.
structure-4: And now the Theatre Remains, the surviving parts of the ancient theatre. Picture the audience settling onto the seats.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the City Walls and the Agora.
facts: Did you know? Comana was known for its school of gladiators and for its sacred attendants, regarded as priestesses of the goddess Ma. It was a temple state: its ruler was the high priest of the goddess Ma, ranked second only to the king. And Strabo puts the number of sacred servants attached to the temple at over six thousand.
outro: This brings our tour of Comana to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for joining us, and enjoy your visit.
